newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas edges higher on western cold.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas edges higher on western cold.

text.p: Canadian spot natgas prices rose slightly in the western markets Tuesday, propped up by below-normal temperatures and stronger power prices in the Northwest, sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices gained about two cents to the C$1.38-1.41 per gigajoule (GJ) range.
"NOVA's drafting, and it's a little cooler today and should be again tomorrow. But then it supposed to turn warmer. This should be short-lived," one Calgary-based trader said.
April AECO prices were still talked around C$1.40 per GJ, while summer prices also hung onto the C$1.40-1.41 level.
At Sumas, Wash., prices rose by more than five cents to the $1.17-1.22 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) area.
Inflating the market, some traders said, was news that Bonneville Power Administration was raising its prices for firm power during peak demand hours on Wednesday by $4.25 per megawatt hour (MWh).
At Niagara, where trading was light, prices were steady in the $2.03-2.08 per mmBtu range.
